title: 4.4 Trigonometry II: heights, ladders, ramps and special angles

q.Q2: Q2. A learner stands 20 m from a flagpole and measures an angle of elevation of 35° to the top. Her eyes are 1.5 m above the ground. Find the height of the pole (tan 35° = 0.700).

q.Q3: Q3. A 6 m ladder leans against a wall making 70° with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach? (sin 70° = 0.940)
q.Q4: Q4. A ramp rises 0.5 m over a horizontal distance of 6 m. Find its angle with the ground (tan⁻¹ 0.0833 = 4.8°) and say whether it suits wheelchairs (about 5° or less).

q.Q5: Q5. Without a calculator, find the height reached by a 10 m ladder making 30° with the ground.
q.Q6: Q6. Why is tan 45° equal to 1?

q.Q7: Q7. A pole is 9 m tall. A stay wire from its top makes 60° with the ground. Find the length of the wire (sin 60° = 0.866).
